purpose: Inspect takes a public GitHub repository address and, optionally, a commit, reads the code at that commit without running any of it, and hands back an inspection report on what it does and how safe it is. The repository may hold an agent, or a plugin or skills for a person's own coding tool (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and others), which runs on that person's machine with their files and their credentials. The report is a list of findings in eight sections, each finding standing on its own and citing a file and line at the commit. Its readers are the person in charge of a department's agents, deciding whether to bring in an outside agent, and an IT, security or team lead deciding whether employees may install a plugin, before anything is installed or given a credential. It judges no fit with anyone's plan, matches the agent to no catalog role and gives no bring-it-in-or-not verdict.

users.who: The person in charge of a department's agents
users.wants: To know what an outside agent does and how safe it is before anything is installed or given a credential.

users.who: An IT, security or team lead
users.wants: When an employee wants to add a plugin to Claude Code or Cursor, or one is found installed: what it adds to people's tools, what it touches and runs on their machines, whether to worry, and what to put in place before allowing it.

users.who: A later agent, such as the future Roadmap agent
users.wants: Sections 3, 4 and 5 of the report as precise, structured findings it can read without guessing.

features.name: Fetch the repository at the commit
features.does: Reads GitHub's record of the repository and of the commit, and the archive of the repository at that commit, with read-only calls, and unpacks the archive into the job's own folder without following any link in it.

inputs.name: repository
inputs.about: The public GitHub repository's address, https://github.com/<owner>/<name>, on a line of the message (repository: ...) or anywhere in it; a message from another agent may give <owner>/<name>, which is read the same way.

inputs.name: commit
inputs.about: The commit's digest, 7 to 40 hexadecimal characters, on a line of the message (commit: ...), or as the last part of a https://github.com/<owner>/<name>/commit/<digest> or /tree/<digest> address that names the repository too; when the message names none, the newest commit on the repository's default branch.

inputs.name: plugin
inputs.about: When the repository holds several plugins, the one to inspect, by the name its manifest or marketplace gives it, on a line of the message (plugin: ...); left blank, the first is inspected and the others are listed.

requirements.shall: The agent shall take the repository as a https://github.com/<owner>/<name> address or as <owner>/<name>, declaring it as an address (kind url, so the Next app links the job's subject to it; 0.4.4) while still reading <owner>/<name> from a message, and the commit, when the message names one, as 7 to 40 hexadecimal characters, from repository: and commit: lines of the message or from one https://github.com/<owner>/<name>/commit/<digest> or /tree/<digest> address that names both.

source.said: Inspect takes a GitHub repository address and a commit

requirements.shall: The agent shall read from GitHub only with GET requests: the repository's record, the commit's record (or, when no commit is named, the record of the newest commit on the default branch), the commits of the last 90 days, and the archive of the repository at that commit.

source.said: GitHub, read only (public repos at a commit)

requirements.shall: The agent shall make at most 6 calls to GitHub in one job, and shall stop with words saying so when GitHub says its allowance for anonymous reads has run out.

source.said: GitHub, read only (public repos at a commit)

requirements.shall: The agent shall take the commit's full 40-character digest from GitHub's record of the commit, and shall mark the commit as checked only when the archive's own header names that same digest.

source.said: Every finding cites a file and line at the commit.

requirements.shall: The agent shall refuse, and inspect nothing, when GitHub has no public repository at the address, saying: There is no public repository at <owner>/<name> on GitHub, so nothing was inspected.

source.said: public repos at a commit

requirements.shall: The agent shall refuse, and inspect nothing, when the commit is not a commit of the repository, saying: <commit> is not a commit of <owner>/<name>, so nothing was inspected.

source.said: Inspect takes a GitHub repository address and a commit

requirements.shall: The agent shall refuse, and inspect nothing, when the repository is missing, saying so, and when the commit is given as a branch or tag name rather than a digest, saying that Inspect reads one commit and a branch or a tag can move.

source.said: Inspect takes a GitHub repository address and a commit

requirements.shall: The agent shall refuse, and inspect nothing, an archive larger than 50 MB or holding more than 20000 files, saying how large it is and the limit it is over.

source.said: reads the agent's code

requirements.shall: The agent shall unpack the archive only inside the job's own folder, shall write no file whose path leaves that folder, shall write no link and follow no link, and shall record each link the archive holds, with its path and where it points, as a fact.

source.said: Read only: it never runs the repo's code.

requirements.shall: The agent shall, when GitHub does not answer or answers with an error, deliver no report and say which call failed and what GitHub answered, so the person can try again later.

source.said: GitHub, read only (public repos at a commit)

requirements.shall: The agent shall, when the message names no commit, read the newest commit on the repository's default branch, as GitHub's record of the repository names that branch, and inspect it, recording its full 40-character digest in the report and saying in what was inspected that it was the newest on that branch; a commit named, or a commit's address, is inspected as named. It shall refuse, and inspect nothing, when the default branch has no commit.

source.said: Why are you mandating a specific commit? wouldn't it just be the last one?

requirements.shall: The agent shall start at most 20 inspections for one asker, and 200 for everyone, in a UTC day, counted in the records folder the host keeps across jobs before anything is read or the model is asked, and shall refuse one over either cap in words that say when to try again; it shall keep who asked only as a digest and the counts for one day at most, and shall refuse when it cannot keep the count.

source.said: Bounded spend: a per-tenant quota and a global daily budget on model consumption, refused at the door (docs/platform-agents.md).

requirements.shall: The agent shall take an optional plugin, by name, on a plugin: line. When the repository holds several plugins it shall inspect the one named, else the first listed, reading only that plugin's files (its folder less any other plugin's folder inside it, or the skills its marketplace entry lists, with the repository's license, readme, marketplaces and manifests), and shall list every plugin the repository holds with whether it is the one inspected. A plugin named that the repository does not hold shall be refused in words naming the ones it holds, and one it lists but keeps in another repository refused naming where; nothing is inspected.

source.said: Teach Inspect to read plugin and skill repositories (the owner, 2026-11-27): a directory with 600,000 open skills and one-line installers into Claude Code, Cursor and Codex means employees will install unvetted code into their tools every day; Inspect reads a plugin or skill repository the same way it reads an agent: what it does, what it touches, and its risks.

acceptance.gherkin:
Scenario: The repository and commit are read from the message
  Given a message with the lines repository: https://github.com/acme/helper and commit: 86d8f66
  When Inspect reads the message
  Then it asks GitHub for acme/helper at 86d8f66 with GET requests only
  And it makes no more than 6 calls to GitHub

Scenario: A commit address names both
  Given a message holding https://github.com/acme/helper/commit/86d8f667796890eb6d3612dbd1b9e941782fe03f
  When Inspect reads the message
  Then the repository is acme/helper and the commit is 86d8f667796890eb6d3612dbd1b9e941782fe03f

Scenario: The archive is the named commit
  Given GitHub's record of commit 86d8f66 gives the full digest 86d8f667796890eb6d3612dbd1b9e941782fe03f
  And the archive's header names the same digest
  When Inspect fetches the archive
  Then the report's commit is the full digest and it is marked as checked

Scenario: No such public repository
  Given GitHub answers 404 for acme/nothing-here
  When Inspect is asked to inspect acme/nothing-here at 86d8f66
  Then it replies There is no public repository at acme/nothing-here on GitHub, so nothing was inspected.
  And it delivers no report

Scenario: The commit is not in the repository
  Given GitHub answers 422 for the commit deadbee of acme/helper
  When Inspect is asked to inspect acme/helper at deadbee
  Then it replies deadbee is not a commit of acme/helper, so nothing was inspected.
  And it delivers no report

Scenario: A branch name instead of a commit
  Given a message with the lines repository: acme/helper and commit: main
  When Inspect reads the message
  Then it replies that Inspect reads one commit and a branch or a tag can move
  And it makes no call to GitHub

Scenario: Nothing to say which repository
  Given a message that names no repository
  When Inspect reads the message
  Then it replies naming the repository as missing
  And it makes no call to GitHub

Scenario: The archive is too large
  Given GitHub says the archive of the commit is 61 MB
  When Inspect fetches it
  Then it replies that the archive is 61 MB and over the limit of 50 MB
  And it delivers no report

Scenario: A link and a path that leaves the folder
  Given an archive holding a link .claude/skills pointing to ../skills and a file whose path climbs out with ../
  When Inspect unpacks it
  Then no file is written outside the job's folder and no link is written
  And the link is recorded as a fact with its path and where it points

Scenario: GitHub fails
  Given GitHub answers 503 to the archive
  When Inspect fetches it
  Then it delivers no report
  And it replies naming the archive call and GitHub's answer 503

Scenario: No commit named
  Given a message with the line repository: https://github.com/acme/helper and no commit
  And GitHub's record of acme/helper names its default branch trunk
  When Inspect reads the message
  Then it asks GitHub for the newest commit on trunk with a GET request
  And it inspects that commit and the report's commit is its full digest
  And what was inspected says it was the newest on trunk
  And it makes no more than 6 calls to GitHub

Scenario: The day is full
  Given 200 inspections have started today
  When one more request names a repository
  Then Inspect refuses it, saying when to try again
  And it makes no call to GitHub and posts nothing to the running job

Scenario: One plugin of several
  Given a repository whose marketplace lists the plugins one and two, kept in its own folders, and far, kept in another repository
  When Inspect is sent the repository with no plugin
  Then it inspects one, reading none of two's files but its manifest, and lists the three plugins, one as this report
  When it is sent plugin: two
  Then it inspects two
  When it is sent plugin: nope
  Then it says the repository holds one, two and far, and inspects nothing

features.name: Read the facts by rule
features.does: Reads the codebase at the commit with the reverse engineer's read-the-codebase scripts and the security reviewer's program trace and credential scan, adds the agent's own parts found by fixed patterns, and gives every fact an id, a file and a line, with no model.

requirements.shall: The agent shall read the codebase with the reverse engineer's read-the-codebase scripts as carried, keeping as facts the environment variables the code reads (by name, never by value, marked as credentials by their names), its entry points and how it starts, its test files and their cases, its test command and the schemas it carries, each with its file and line.

source.said: Inspect reuses the reverse engineer's fact-gathering skills: read-the-codebase, list-the-dependencies (including the CycloneDX SBOM), check-the-evidence, and the scripts those skills run.

requirements.shall: The agent shall read each program with the security reviewer's program trace as carried, keeping as facts each network address a program calls or writes down, each call to an address it is handed, each command it starts and each browser it drives, each with its file and line.

source.said: The security reviewer has the reach / spend / never-do shape; borrow its vocabulary for section 7.

requirements.shall: The agent shall keep as facts, by fixed patterns, each skill (a folder holding SKILL.md, with the name and description its front matter gives), each model the code names and the setting or line that chooses it, each tool the code hands a model, each place the code stops for a person, each place it keeps memory between jobs, each script that runs at install, and each license file, with its file and line.

source.said: Scripts collect the facts; the model writes only the judgments

requirements.shall: The agent shall decide by rule, for each skill folder and for each script that runs as a command together with the files it imports from its own folder, whether it can be lifted out on its own: it can when every import in its code resolves inside its own folder or to the language's own modules, it reads no credential from its environment, and it loads or installs no package at run time; the fact names each import, credential or run-time package that keeps it from standing alone, and each other setting it reads.

source.said: its skills as separate parts, and whether each can be lifted out on its own

requirements.shall: The agent shall find committed credentials with the security reviewer's credential scan as carried, and shall keep for each only its file, its line and what kind of credential it looks like, never the matched characters.

source.said: committed secrets

requirements.shall: The agent shall give each fact an id of the form F followed by four or more digits, its kind, its file and line at the commit when it has one, and the text of that line exactly as written when the line is at most 400 characters long, and shall say a longer line's length instead of cutting its text.

source.said: Every finding cites a file and line at the commit.

requirements.shall: The agent shall, when the archive holds no file it can read as text, still write the report with sections 2 and 8, and section 8 shall say that there was no code to read.

source.said: reads the agent's code

requirements.shall: The agent shall tell by rule what the repository holds: a plugin, from a plugin manifest (Agent Plugins 1.0.0's plugin.json naming its 1.0.0 schema; .claude-plugin/plugin.json; .cursor-plugin/plugin.json; .codex-plugin/plugin.json; another tool's .<tool>-plugin/plugin.json; gemini-extension.json) or a marketplace (.claude-plugin/marketplace.json, .cursor-plugin/marketplace.json, .agents/plugins/marketplace.json); skills alone, when SKILL.md files stand with no manifest and no agent code of its own; else an agent, read exactly as before, a Common Agent package among them. Several manifests of one folder are one plugin, packaged for each of their tools.

source.said: Teach Inspect to read plugin and skill repositories (the owner, 2026-11-27): a directory with 600,000 open skills and one-line installers into Claude Code, Cursor and Codex means employees will install unvetted code into their tools every day; Inspect reads a plugin or skill repository the same way it reads an agent: what it does, what it touches, and its risks.

requirements.shall: The agent shall keep as facts, for the plugin inspected, each of its manifests, each command and sub-agent (and each of Cursor's rules) with its size and the tools it may use, each hook with what starts it, what it runs and what the code it runs (followed through the files it imports) calls, starts and touches, each MCP server with how it runs (a program it starts, or an address it connects to), the package it fetches and whether that is pinned, how it signs in and the settings it names, each value the plugin asks the person for, and, in its scripts, reading the home folder, stored credentials or the whole environment and downloading code to run; it shall keep the names of settings and headers, never their values, and shall leave out a SKILL.md its tools never load.

source.said: Teach Inspect to read plugin and skill repositories (the owner, 2026-11-27): a directory with 600,000 open skills and one-line installers into Claude Code, Cursor and Codex means employees will install unvetted code into their tools every day; Inspect reads a plugin or skill repository the same way it reads an agent: what it does, what it touches, and its risks.

acceptance.gherkin:
Scenario: Settings and credentials by name
  Given a codebase whose src/app.py reads os.environ["ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"] on line 12

  When Inspect reads the facts

Scenario: The agent's own parts

  When Inspect reads the facts
  Then each of these is a fact of its own kind with its file and line

Scenario: Which parts can be lifted out
  Given tools/lint.mjs that imports node:fs and ./helpers.mjs, and tools/helpers.mjs that reads the setting LINT_DIR with a default
  And skills/render/scripts/render.mjs that imports ../../../src/shared.mjs
  And tools/report.mjs that reads the credential REPORT_API_KEY
  And tools/load.mjs that loads a package whose name it works out at run time
  When Inspect reads the facts

Scenario: A committed key is never repeated
  Given a file config/dev.env whose line 3 holds an AWS access key
  When Inspect reads the facts

  And neither the facts nor the report hold the key's characters

Scenario: A long line is not cut
  Given a fact whose line is 900 characters long
  When Inspect writes the fact
  Then the fact gives the line's length as 900 and no part of its text

Scenario: Nothing to read
  Given an archive whose only file is a picture
  When Inspect writes the report
  Then the report holds sections 2 and 8
  And section 8 says there was no code to read

Scenario: Each shape by its own files
  Given a Claude Code plugin also packaged for Cursor, an Agent Plugins 1.0.0 plugin, a Codex plugin, a Cursor plugin with a rule, two folders of skills alone, and an agent's repository with skills beside its own code
  When Inspect reads each
  Then each is told by its own files, the first as one plugin for Claude Code and Cursor, and the last as an agent

Scenario: What a plugin adds
  Given a plugin with a command that may run shell commands, a sub-agent, a session-start hook whose program imports one that calls an outside address and reads the home folder, a hook that asks a model, a hook that sends events to an address, an MCP server fetched by npx with no version and one at an address with a key in a header, a key it asks for, and a script that reads stored AWS credentials
  When Inspect reads the facts
  Then each is a fact of its own kind with its file and line
  And the hook says when a session starts or resumes, the files it runs and the address the imported file calls
  And no fact or finding holds the header's value

features.name: List the dependencies and check them against OSV
features.does: Makes a CycloneDX 1.5 dependency list by rule with the reverse engineer's list-the-dependencies script, adds the packages of a uv.lock, and asks OSV which of the exactly versioned packages have known vulnerabilities.

outputs.name: sbom
outputs.about: The dependency list as a CycloneDX 1.5 bill of materials, made by rule and never by the model: every component with its version, its package URL and where it was read.

requirements.shall: The agent shall make the dependency list as a CycloneDX 1.5 bill of materials with the reverse engineer's list-the-dependencies script as carried, and shall add each package a uv.lock names, with its version and package URL, to the same list.

source.said: list-the-dependencies (including the CycloneDX SBOM)

requirements.shall: The agent shall ask OSV about every component with an exact version in the npm, PyPI, Go or crates.io ecosystems, by queries that read and write nothing, at most 1000 components a query and at most 10 queries a job, and shall then read each vulnerability found, at most 60 a job.

source.said: OSV (osv.dev), read only, for known holes in dependencies

requirements.shall: The agent shall write each known vulnerability as a finding of section 7 naming the package, its version, the OSV id and its aliases, the version that fixes it when OSV gives one, the line of the manifest or lockfile the package was read from, the level OSV's record gives, and the categories LLM03:2025 Supply Chain and ASI04 Agentic Supply Chain Vulnerabilities.

source.said: known holes in dependencies

requirements.shall: The agent shall list as findings of section 8 the components it could not ask OSV about (a version range rather than a version, an ecosystem OSV is not asked for, a lockfile neither reader reads) and the vulnerabilities over the limit of 60 by id alone.

source.said: what Inspect could not settle without running it

requirements.shall: The agent shall, when OSV does not answer or answers with an error, still deliver the report, with a finding of section 8 saying the dependencies were not checked against OSV and what OSV answered.

source.said: OSV (osv.dev), read only, for known holes in dependencies

acceptance.gherkin:
Scenario: The dependency list
  Given a codebase with a package-lock.json naming left-pad 1.3.0 and a uv.lock naming httpx 0.27.0
  When Inspect lists the dependencies
  Then sbom.cdx.json is a CycloneDX 1.5 bill of materials holding pkg:npm/left-pad@1.3.0 and pkg:pypi/httpx@0.27.0

Scenario: A known vulnerability
  Given OSV says GHSA-aaaa-bbbb-cccc affects httpx 0.27.0, with the alias CVE-2026-0001, severity HIGH and a fix in 0.27.2
  When Inspect checks the dependencies
  Then section 7 holds a finding naming httpx 0.27.0, GHSA-aaaa-bbbb-cccc, CVE-2026-0001, the fix 0.27.2 and the uv.lock line
  And its level is high and its categories are LLM03:2025 and ASI04

Scenario: What could not be asked
  Given a package.json with no lockfile asking for express ^4.0.0
  When Inspect checks the dependencies
  Then section 8 says express was not checked because only a range is given

Scenario: OSV fails
  Given OSV answers 500
  When Inspect checks the dependencies
  Then the report is still delivered
  And section 8 says the dependencies were not checked against OSV and that OSV answered 500

features.name: Write the judgments
features.does: Gives a model the facts and asks it for the judgments of sections 3 to 8 and then section 1, in up to three model calls a job, each citing the facts it rests on, and keeps only the judgments the reverse engineer's check-the-evidence scripts and the published lists let through.

requirements.shall: The agent shall give the model the facts the scripts found, whole, and in parts when they are more than one call can take, and shall ask it only for judgments, each citing by id one or more of those facts.

source.said: the model writes only the judgments, and each judgment cites a fact the scripts found

requirements.shall: The agent shall hold back a judgment that cites no fact, or cites a fact the scripts did not find, or whose evidence does not check against the commit with the reverse engineer's evidence check, or that is a risk resting only on known flaws OSV has already rated (each package has its own finding for them), and shall list each one held back with the reason.

source.said: check-the-evidence

requirements.shall: The agent shall hold back a judgment of section 3, 4 or 5 whose words judge the code or infer beyond what the facts show, by the reverse engineer's lists of such words.

source.said: Sections 3, 4 and 5 must be precise, because the future Roadmap agent reads them.

requirements.shall: The agent shall give every risk a level from the CVSS v4.0 qualitative severity rating scale (none, low, medium, high, critical) and a category from the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025 (LLM01:2025 to LLM10:2025) or the OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications (ASI01 to ASI10), and shall hold back a risk without both or with a category from no list.

source.said: Each risk carries a level and a category from a published list: the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications and OWASP's agentic AI threats list, SPDX license names, and a CycloneDX dependency list.

requirements.shall: The agent shall hold back any judgment that gives a verdict on whether to bring the agent in, or that judges its fit with a plan or matches it to a catalog role.

source.said: No recommendation: it gives no bring-it-in-or-not verdict.

requirements.shall: The agent shall write section 1 last, from the findings of sections 2 to 8: at most 5 findings, each naming the finding it repeats and carrying that finding's evidence.

source.said: At a glance | The few findings that matter most, written last

requirements.shall: The agent shall set an output budget on every model call and read why the answer ended, and shall treat an answer that stopped at its budget as a failure that says so, never as a whole answer.

source.said: a model for the judgments, through the shared model caller (Common Agent 12.4.1, system of kind model)

requirements.shall: The agent shall, when the model fails or stops at its budget, still deliver the report with the scripts' findings, and each section the model would have judged shall hold a finding saying the judgment was not made and why.

source.said: Scripts collect the facts; the model writes only the judgments

requirements.shall: The agent shall decide whether a person must supply each outside system by rule, the same in every run of the same commit, from the settings the system reads and where the code that reaches it is: a setting its own code stops without is required; one it skips a feature without, or has a default for, is optional; one read plainly is what the setup docs say, else optional when the example settings file leaves it commented out; one read only inside its skills is optional; one only its tests read is never needed. A system with a required setting is required, and one whose settings are all optional, or that only its skills reach, is optional; one it reads no setting for, where the person has nothing to set up, is said as nothing to set up and never counted as required. Only where these leave it unclear does the model's answer stand, and the report keeps the model's answer either way.

source.said: The count of required systems varied from run to run because the model judged it.

requirements.shall: The agent shall give its model no line that AgentMesh's screening has not passed first: before the first two calls, each fact line those calls would read, exactly as they would read it, and before the last call, each finding line it would read, sent to the platform's screening door (POST /v1/screen-text) signed with the job's own credential. A line the screening holds or flags shall be left out of what the model reads, and the passages held from the first two calls shall be one risk of section 7, by rule, high when the screening read any of them as instructions aimed at an AI and medium otherwise, citing them and quoting none of them.

source.said: A malicious repository could steer Inspect's model into calling itself safe, so this must be fixed before prod (the coordinator, 2026-11-26).

requirements.shall: The agent shall fail closed: when the job has no credential or platform address, the screening cannot be reached, answers anything but a verdict for every passage, or could not check a passage itself, the model shall be given nothing, the report shall still be delivered with the scripts' findings, and each section the model would have judged shall say the judgment was not made and why. A request that could not be reached, answered 5xx or could not check a passage is asked once more; a refusal is not.

source.said: A malicious repository could steer Inspect's model into calling itself safe, so this must be fixed before prod (the coordinator, 2026-11-26).

requirements.shall: The agent shall tell the model, for a plugin or skills, what it is and that it runs inside the person's own tool, on their machine, with their files and their credentials, ask it for each hook's plain words, and hold back a risk that rests only on hooks, whose risk is the scripts'; an agent's prompts shall be as before.

source.said: Teach Inspect to read plugin and skill repositories (the owner, 2026-11-27): a directory with 600,000 open skills and one-line installers into Claude Code, Cursor and Codex means employees will install unvetted code into their tools every day; Inspect reads a plugin or skill repository the same way it reads an agent: what it does, what it touches, and its risks.

requirements.shall: The agent shall, for a plugin or skills, tell the model never to state how many skills, commands, sub-agents, hooks, MCP servers, scripts, tests, files or lines it has, and shall take any such count of two or more out of the model's words (the description, section 1 and every judgment), so the report's own counts are the only ones.

source.said: The coordinator's review of 0.5.6 (2026-11-27): the Overview's words said four slash commands while the tile said 5; the tiles must be the only counts. Telemetry was said on the session-start hook row and again as a row of its own; say each fact once.

requirements.shall: The agent shall, by rule from the code alone, (a) record each place the code checks for a system it reads no setting for (a program on the PATH, a daemon that answers, a stop whose words say a program is not installed) and whether it stops there; (b) record each stop in the agent's own code whose message names two or more alternatives, each a system or a setting, with what is missing in its words; (c) decide that such a stop is on the path the agent's commands share when its function is called, through an import of its module, from an entry file and another file of its own code (or one step further); (d) for each such stop write one system finding by script, Required, naming each alternative and what the person supplies for it; (e) mark each system the model wrote that is one of the alternatives (by a setting it names, or by its name): said only in the group when it reads no setting of its own beyond the group's, else kept with its own need, never Required by the model's word alone, and never saying it can be left out; (f) make a probed system Required when the code stops without it on that shared path. A stop off the shared path makes no group. (g) 0.7.3: when the agent's own code calls a model, it needs a model provider: the makers of the models its own code names are one required group by rule (one maker named makes that maker's system required by rule), whose members are the systems that cite a model or say they are a model or provider, never an image or speech service of the same maker.

features.name: Write the report
features.does: Writes the inspection report as a list of findings grouped in the eight sections, each standing on its own, through one place that emits a finding, with the dependency list beside it and a short reply.

outputs.name: inspection
outputs.about: The inspection report in the inspection-report-v1 format: the repository and commit, the eight sections, the findings in section order, the judgments held back with why, the facts the findings cite, and what the job used. While the job runs, a working copy of it with the findings so far is posted under the same name, marked partial.

partial.description: only on the working copy posted while the job runs, never on the delivered report: the stage the job is at, how many findings so far, how many are left out of this copy to keep it one piece, and whether their words are

sha.description: the commit's full digest; null only in the first working copy, posted before GitHub's record names the commit

checked.description: true when the archive's own header named this digest

text.description: the line exactly as written at the commit, when it is at most 400 characters

long_line.description: the line's length, given instead of its text when it is longer than 400 characters

call.description: the read-only call the fact came from, such as GET /repos/{owner}/{name}

level_by.description: who set the level: the record it came from (OSV), a fixed rule of Inspect's (a committed credential is high), or the model

detail.description: fields of the finding's kind: a skill's name, path, description, scripts and lift_out (yes or no) with the imports that keep it from standing alone, its size (scripts, lines of code, the length of its instructions and the tests that name it) and its instructions as text (instructions, up to 8,000 characters each and 250,000 in all; instructions_cut when shortened, with instructions_address, the file at the commit on GitHub); the agent's own code's files and lines; a job's does; a risk's safe, how to make it safe; a model's name, where it is chosen and whether a setting changes it; a system's name, host, access (read, write, read-write or unknown), the credentials it expects, need (required, optional, unclear, or none when the person has nothing to set up), supply (what the person supplies), without (what happens without it) and sends (what goes to it); since 0.4.0 need is decided by rule from the settings it reads and where the code that reaches it is (need_by rule, with need_why and need_settings), and the model's own answer stands only where they leave it unclear (need_by model), kept as need_by_model either way; a credential's need, need_by and need_why by the same rule; a tool's name, what it does and whether it runs without a person's OK; a vulnerability's package, version, OSV id, aliases and fixed version

FindingSoFar.description: a finding in the working copy: its id, place, title and level, the first place it cites, the fields of its detail the view draws, and its words where they fit

level_by.description: who set the level: the record it came from (OSV), a fixed rule of Inspect's (a committed credential is high), or the model

more_evidence.description: how many more places the finding cites in the delivered report

detail.description: the fields of the finding's detail the view draws while the job runs (0.4.0): what was inspected, a skill's size, the agent's own code, the count of tests, a system's need and what the person supplies, a credential's need, a risk's fix; left out when the copy does not fit

outputs.name: inspection-md

features.name: Say how tied it is to its platform, and what moving it would take
features.does: From a copy of AgentMesh's agent platforms database pinned to one AgentMesh commit, reads by rule which platforms the code is built on, which of their features it uses at each file and line, and the open standards it uses; and from those alone says, for each category it uses, what it uses and how open that is, and, for every other platform, the work to move it, what it would lose and what replaces each part, in the database's own words, with no recommendation.

requirements.shall: The agent shall carry AgentMesh's agent platforms database (data/agent-platforms) byte for byte at one AgentMesh commit, recording that commit, the date its entries were checked and the sha256 of every file, so that updating it is a normal pull request.

source.said: Add a portability reading to the Inspect agent (the owner, 2026-11-27, through the coordinator): how tied an agent is to its platform, and what moving it elsewhere would take and cost; "we'd need to also state what you might be missing if you do the switch, like LangGraph is associated with Evals, Key Stores, Telemetry", and "what each destination provides, this is important". The aim is to show buyers how open an agent really is, fairly.

requirements.shall: The agent shall count a platform only from its packages in the manifests (development dependencies aside), its modules in the code's imports (a module the repository holds being its own), a config file only that platform names, or the frameworks its dependencies name; and a feature of it only from that feature's evidence in the database, at its file and line: an import with one of the names it or its cell's own words give, a call or a code key only in a file that imports that platform, a setting, file, config key or command only once the platform counts; never in a comment, a docstring, a test, a lockfile or a folder kept for coding assistants; and never a feature the platform merely offers.

Tests and gaps shall answer first in one line, then list each item in one line with its words behind it.

source.said: The owner, 2026-11-27, through the coordinator, on Inspect's report on dev: "Rename the tab 'Could it move?' to 'Portability'"; at its top, how well the agent follows AgentMesh's portability guidance for builders ("you don't get a feel for if it's adhering to so many of the items we mentioned in our portability document. It doesn't need to be exhaustive, but we should give some indication"); "I don't want AgentMesh to be a target - that's not our business"; 'Moving it' becomes 'Run it in', the organization's preferred harnesses ("we should probably have a section for your preferred harnesses and if they haven't picked one yet, they'd have a button to identify and set it up"); "Improve the formatting for the Tests and Gaps tab content"; and the coordinator's yes to debt 939 (each evidence item carries its own openness).

requirements.shall: A maker's preview or beta label shall not lower a harness capability's rating, as the platforms data already rules (the database re-pinned with its harness cells following it); each harness card shall draw its maker's mark where one exists (OpenAI's for ChatGPT, Codex and the Agents API, opencode's own), never a letter; and in a list on the page a comma shall never start a line, nor split one item over two lines.

source.said: The coordinator, 2026-11-27: the harness list counts beta as Partly while the platforms data does not lower a rating for beta (follow the platforms data); 'O' letter icons for ChatGPT and opencode; the comma wrap in destination lists on the Portability and Run it in lines.

acceptance.gherkin:
Scenario: The database is pinned
  Given the copy in assets/agent-platforms
  Then every file's sha256 is the one pinned.json names, at a 40-character AgentMesh commit
  And the database's date is its oldest entry's

Scenario: A LangGraph agent
  Given a LangGraph agent that uses LangSmith's sandboxes and tracing and LangGraph's checkpoints, with a comment, a test and a coding assistant's folder that name other features
  When Inspect reads it
  Then it is built on LangChain's stack
  And each row cites its file and line, the sandbox at its import, not the docstring above it
  And evaluations and deployment are not used

Scenario: Names that are not the platform's
  Given a package of its own named agents, and a class of its own named Memory
  Then neither OpenAI nor Mastra counts
  And comments and docstrings are never read as code

Scenario: Moving it
  Given an agent that scores its runs with LangSmith
  Then every other platform is a destination, AgentMesh first and three shown
  And each destination's cells are its own ratings and words
  And AgentMesh's none for evaluations is what it would lose, as any platform's none is

Scenario: A plugin
  Given a Claude Code plugin
  Then its rows are packaging, its MCP servers, its hooks and its commands
  And the other ten categories are said not to apply
  And no destination has a runtime to re-host

Scenario: What it needs
  Given an agent that reaches LangSmith's sandboxes
  Then the first call asks what each outside service is needed for, naming its facts, and the second does not
  And a plain answer citing facts is kept, and one with a path, advice or no fact is held back

Scenario: The report
  Given an inspection of such an agent
  Then the report carries the reading with its evidence and fits its schema
  And the Markdown says it after Systems it uses, each place a link to its line, with the database's commit and date
  And the working copy carries it without the evidence

Scenario: A working copy short of room
  Given more findings than fit
  Then the database's words go first, then the reading, and each system's need is kept

Scenario: The tab
  Given a delivered report with a reading
  Then Portability follows Systems it uses, opens on what it is built on and the services it reaches, draws each row in a word and a shape, opens the database's words in a dialog, keeps the reading through a copy that leaves it out, and names no file of the repository

Scenario: Openness by evidence
  Given a LangGraph agent that loads skills through create_deep_agent's skills argument
  Then its packaging reads as open as Agent Skills, and langgraph.json reads as LangChain's own

Scenario: The guidance's basics
  Given a repository with plugin.json, skills in skills/<name>/SKILL.md, an unpinned npx tool server, no AGENTS.md and a lock file
  Then the basics say followed, missing or not known by rule, and a release GitHub did not answer for is not known

Scenario: Harness cards read cleanly
  Given the preferred harnesses opencode, ChatGPT and Codex
  When the view draws Run it in
  Then each card's icon is its maker's mark, not a letter
  And each item of a list on the Portability tab keeps its comma with it on one line

constraints.shall: The agent shall never run, install, build or test the repository's code, shall call no write action on any system, and shall write files only inside the job's own folders.

source.said: Read only: it never runs the repo's code. Inspect calls no write action anywhere.

constraints.shall: The agent shall take out anything that looks like a credential from everything it hands the model, writes in the report or says in its reply, with the security reviewer's scrub as carried.

source.said: committed secrets

constraints.shall: The agent shall carry the reverse engineer's and the security reviewer's scripts and the shared model caller byte for byte, each named in reused.json with its repository, its commit and the sha256 of its bytes, and a test shall fail when a carried script no longer matches its pin.

source.said: The owner wants these shared, pinned to a version, not forked.

constraints.shall: The agent shall run on Node 22 or later with nothing outside Node, and shall reach its model only through the shared model caller and the model's four settings.

source.said: a model for the judgments, through the shared model caller (Common Agent 12.4.1, system of kind model)

constraints.shall: The agent shall never cut content without saying so: what is over a limit is handed on in parts, or is named in the report with the limit it is over.

source.said: The report is a list of findings, each standing on its own

constraints.shall: The agent shall reach AgentMesh's screening only with the credential and the platform address the platform gives the job (MESH_JOB_JWT, MESH_JOB_NKEY_SEED, MESH_API_BASE), shall never send it to another address, and shall treat a missing one as a screening that cannot answer.

source.said: Prefer a platform path every packaged agent can use, over something special to Inspect (the coordinator, 2026-11-26).

systems.name: code-host
systems.why: GitHub: the repository record, the commit record, its recent commits and the archive of the repository at the commit, read with GET requests only and no key, because only public repositories are inspected.

systems.name: vulnerability-database
systems.why: OSV (osv.dev): which exact versions of the dependencies have known vulnerabilities, asked by queries that change nothing, and the record of each vulnerability found, with no key.

settings.name: GITHUB_API
settings.about: where GitHub's API answers, its base address

settings.name: OSV_API
settings.about: where the OSV API answers, its base address
